stages.name: First Light — The Story Run
stages.note: Twelve trophies are tied by their official descriptions to named missions and chapters, so the story comes first and unlocks everything else [1][2]. The campaign runs five chapters and roughly 60–80 hours [3].

stages.name: Open Roads — Early Free-Roam Habits
stages.note: Partner play opens during Chapter 2, and the descriptions behind the partner, meditation and money trophies all become workable in free-roam from then on [3][4]. Habits started here — scanning vehicles, meditating, registering cars — pay off again in the checklist stage [3][5].

stages.name: The Long Ledger — The 100% Checklist
stages.note: After the final mission the 100% Completion checklist opens under Progress > Stats, and its lines count exactly what these descriptions count: stunts, medals, card sets, scans and robberies [3][4][5]. This is the long stage every roadmap agrees on [3][5].

stages.name: Strangers & Loose Ends
stages.note: The named side-story finales are not part of the 100% checklist, so they wait until it is done; their quest givers stay available after the story, which is what makes this order safe [3][4].

stages.name: The Platinum Pop
stages.note: The platinum needs nothing of its own: its official description is simply that you are a Leonida Legend once every other trophy is earned [1][2].

groundRules: One playthrough is enough: the guides agree on a single minimum playthrough, free-roam after the story, and no mission replay [3][5].
Keep manual saves: the game offers 15 manual slots plus one autosave — park one at the start of each chapter and one untouched save before the final mission [3][4].
No difficulty gate and no online gate: there are no difficulty settings tied to trophies and all 55 trophies are offline, single-player [3][5].
Never use cheats on a trophy save: turning a cheat on disables trophies and saving [3][7].
Take the Chapter 1 balcony meditation when Lucia offers it — it cannot be replayed once the chapter closes [3][4].

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.summary: The platinum itself: it lands on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned.

steps.text: Treat this as the finish line, not a task: it unlocks automatically once every other trophy in the base list is yours [1][2].
No multiplayer and no DLC are involved — the whole list is single-player and offline [3][5].
When one trophy is left standing, use the Next up line in the Ledger and the last roadmap stage to pick the fastest finisher [3][4].

trophies.deeper: Because the platinum needs all 54 others, its real guide is the roadmap: story first, the 100% checklist second, strangers and leftovers last. Nothing on the way can lock you out as long as the one possibly-missable meditation is handled back in Chapter 1 [3][4].

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.summary: The long gold: finish the in-game 100% Completion checklist, which only opens after the story.

steps.text: Finish the story first; the checklist then appears under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion, and progress made earlier already counts [3][4].
Work the big blocks the checklist demands in full: all robberies, 300 stunts, 70 of 80 challenges, all 42 shooting-range golds and all 42 drone time trials [3][5].
Collect only what the checklist asks for: scan 200 of 277 base-model vehicles, study 100 of 255 animals, finish 15 of 18 card sets [3][5].
Fill the remaining gaps with optional missions — the checklist wants 100 and far more than that exist [3][5].

trophies.deeper: Every guide stresses that the checklist is lenient — roughly 60% of everything in the game — so stop each activity once its checklist line is full instead of clearing the whole map [3][5]. The guides do disagree on the hours: most put the full platinum near 200 hours, while Push Square warns to set aside up to 300 or more [3][6].
